proof.criterion: The review's blocking authz finding: a cookie server with no DISPATCH_SIGNIN_* setting must refuse the session cookies an earlier sign-in minted, and must not let one of them act as its person.
proof.surface: Two real envoy-dispatch binaries built by me from this head — the head's own, and one with the new guard disabled (`if false && boot.SignInIssuer == "" && !boot.DevSignIn`, built then reverted with jj restore) — each a process on the rootless Postgres 17.11 with pgvector I rebuilt at 127.0.0.1:5433, both against the same database, which carries the people and user_sessions rows a sign-in leaves behind, driven over HTTP with curl.
proof.command: Minted the cookie with a throwaway cmd/zztestercookie calling auth.IssueSessionCookie(email, 0, auth.ParseSigningKeys(key), false); seeded insert into people (email) values ('someone@example.com') and insert into user_sessions (login) values ('someone@example.com') (select login, generation → someone@example.com|0); booted the fixed binary on 18790 and the unfixed one on 18794 under env -i with the same DATABASE_URL, DISPATCH_AGENT_TOKEN, DISPATCH_SIGNING_KEY, DISPATCH_INSECURE_COOKIE=1, DISPATCH_LISTEN_HOST, DISPATCH_PORT and DISPATCH_SERVER_URL and no DISPATCH_SIGNIN_* at all; then, with that one cookie and no bearer, GET /api/v1/whoami, GET /api/v1/inbox and POST /api/v1/me/agent-tokens with the matching Origin header against each.
proof.observed: On the head's binary every one of the three is HTTP/1.1 401 {"code":"NO_IDENTITY","error":"unauthorized"}: the cookie names nobody, the human-only route is closed, and no personal token is minted. The server's own access log records the request as caller_kind=anonymous.
proof.negativeControl: Two controls, in both directions. (1) The defect, reproduced: the same cookie, the same database and the same three requests against the binary with the guard disabled answer 200 {"kind":"user","login":"someone@example.com"}, 200 [] on the human-only inbox, and 201 on POST /api/v1/me/agent-tokens, which returns a usable dsp_ personal token and leaves a row in agent_tokens. That is the escalation the reviewer named — a stale cookie minting a credential that outlives it — driven on the real surface; the guard is what stops it. (2) The guard is scoped, not a blanket cookie kill: a dev sign-in server from the same fixed binary (DISPATCH_DEV_SIGNIN=1, no sign-in settings, loopback) issues its own cookie at GET /auth/_dev/signin?login=someone@example.com and then answers that cookie 200 {"kind":"user","login":"someone@example.com"} on /api/v1/whoami and 200 on the human-only /api/v1/inbox, so the DevSignIn arm of the condition is live and the cookie path still names its person where it must.

proof.surface: The head's own envoy-dispatch binary as a process on the rebuilt real Postgres, driven over HTTP with curl under env -i.
proof.command: The 18790 boot above, then curl against /healthz, /api/v1/whoami with the agent token, /auth/start, and POST /api/v1/projects with an actor envelope.
proof.observed: /healthz 200 with "signin":null; GET /api/v1/whoami with the agent token 200 {"kind":"agent","owner":null,"service":null}; GET /auth/start 503 {"code":"SIGNIN_UNCONFIGURED",...}; POST /api/v1/projects 201 {"key":"R2P","name":"Round two probe",...}, so the agent API serves writes and not reads alone.
proof.negativeControl: The same binary with the sign-in settings whole is a different server: it logs 'signing people in with Google for a Workspace domain', /healthz answers "signin":true and GET /auth/start answers 302 to accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth with redirect_uri …/auth/callback, so the 503 above is the empty sign-in set's doing. (On that server the fabricated cookie is also refused 401, by the membership check rather than by the new guard: the person it names has no recorded sign-in for Membership to confirm. That is expected and is not what proves the configured path; the dev sign-in control in the row above is.)
